key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current govern molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld-process optimization for low-expansion Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Analysis across laser power, welding speed, and current ranges.
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size; across 0.5–0.8 m/min, higher speed reduced penetration and width; across 150–170 A, higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends within limited parameter ranges but provides no quantitative model-validation errors or weld mechanical-property results.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
